implementation_statement: The vendors provide account functions; the owner creates and removes accounts. SYS-01 has two accounts: the owner (administrator) and the irrigation dealer's technician (full irrigation control since 2024). Gaps: the dealer account has never been reviewed and stays on all year; the laptop has one administrator account shared with family members; no periodic account review.
evidence: EV-001 (SYS-01 user list); EV-020 (laptop user settings)

implementation_statement: SYS-01 enforces its roles (administrator, irrigation technician, viewer). Only the administrator and irrigation technician roles can start, stop, or schedule irrigation. The owner assigns the roles.
evidence: EV-001 (SYS-01 role settings); EV-007 (vendor SOC 2 report; reviewed in P09)

implementation_statement: Compensating control (one-person business): the owner-operator holds every role and there is no bookkeeper. The bank requires a one-time code before a new payee is added, and POL-01 9.5 requires a call-back on a number already on file before any payee's bank details change. The tax preparer (CPA) works from SYS-09 exports each year for Schedule F. POL-01 6.3 limits the irrigation dealer to the viewer role except during a service window the owner opens. Gap: the dealer account still has full irrigation control until POAM-003 is closed.
evidence: EV-017 (bank payee settings); EV-024 (Schedule F prepared by the tax preparer); POL-01 6.3 and 9.5; POAM-003

implementation_statement: Gaps: the dealer's technician account can change any schedule and setpoint at both sites although the dealer only needs read access between service visits; family members use the laptop with administrator rights. Plan: viewer role for the dealer except during an owner-approved service window; separate standard user accounts on the laptop (2026-09-30).
evidence: EV-001 (SYS-01 role settings); EV-020 (laptop user settings)

implementation_statement: All remote control of the pump and pivot goes through SYS-01 over the vendor's connection; no device has an inbound port open to the internet (router check 2026-07-16). Gaps: the dealer's remote control rights are always on with no usage rules, and the vendor's support access setting is on permanently. The dealer agreement has no security terms.
evidence: EV-001 (SYS-01 user list and support access setting); EV-008 (dealer agreement); EV-AC-17 (P07 router port check)

implementation_statement: Home Wi-Fi uses WPA2 with a passphrase. Gap: the farm-stand customer Wi-Fi password is posted at the stand and the customer network is the same network as the laptop and the pump controller's Wi-Fi bridge. Plan: guest network isolation and a separate network for the pump house (2026-11-15).
evidence: EV-022 (router settings); EV-009 (Wi-Fi password posted at the stand)

implementation_statement: The owner has learned security only from vendor videos. The owner will complete a free small-business cybersecurity course and subscribe to monthly reminders by 2026-11-30, and will brief family members who use the laptop.
evidence: EV-029 (no security course on record); course certificate (planned)

Starting 2026-10, the owner reviews all three on the first Monday of each month, and weekly in freeze season, and notes the review in the security log.
evidence: EV-003 (SYS-01 activity log screen); EV-011 (booking sign-in history); EV-016 (email sign-in history); review log (planned)

implementation_statement: Compensating control (one-person business): the owner is the only administrator, so the logs stay with the vendors. SYS-01 keeps its activity log of sign-ins and irrigation commands on the FMIS vendor's platform, and the email and booking platforms keep sign-in history on theirs. No log is kept only on the shared laptop.
evidence: EV-003 (SYS-01 activity log screen); EV-007 (FMIS vendor SOC 2 report; reviewed in P09)

implementation_statement: Compensating control (one-person business): the P07 plan states openly that independence is limited, because the owner designed, operates, and assessed the controls with help from the on-call IT technician. POL-01 4.5 requires a review by someone outside the farm, such as the IT technician or an extension or industry cyber program, at least every second year. The FMIS vendor's SOC 2 Type 2 report, reviewed 2026-07-15, covers the vendor's inherited controls. Gap: the first outside review has not taken place.
evidence: P07 assessment plan; POL-01 4.5; EV-007 (FMIS vendor SOC 2 report); P09 review

implementation_statement: Compensating control (one-person business): there is no change board, so under CM-3(g) the owner is the change control element. POL-01 7.8 requires every change to irrigation schedules, setpoints, fertigation rates, and freeze-alarm thresholds to go in a change log with the date, who made it, and why. POL-01 6.3 requires dealer changes to be logged too. The SYS-01 activity log gives a second record of irrigation commands. Gap: the dealer can still change settings at any time until POAM-003 is closed.
evidence: POL-01 6.3 and 7.8; change log; EV-003 (SYS-01 activity log)

implementation_statement: The owner knows the devices, but there was no written list before this plan. Section 9 of the SSP and POL-01 Appendix A now list each system and device; firmware versions and default-password status of the OT devices still need to be recorded.
evidence: SSP section 9; POL-01 Appendix A; EV-008 (dealer handover device list); EV-030 (no device list before this plan)

implementation_statement: The BIA (P05), POL-01 section 11, and the P08 runbook form the contingency plan. Gaps: the written freeze-night procedure, the mutual-aid arrangement with a neighbor, the standalone freeze alarm, and the sealed recovery codes are not in place yet (due 2026-11-30).
